title: Read a stack frame
description:
Tools print stack frames in the form `module!function+0xOFFSET`, for example `game.exe!Player::update+0x2a`. When symbols are missing, the function part is absent: `game.exe+0x35f10`.

Write `parseFrame(text)`, returning the module, the function (empty if absent) and the offset as a number. The offset is hexadecimal, written with `0x`, in either case. If the text does not fit the form (no `+0x`, nothing before it, no hex digits after it), return `std::nullopt`.

```
"game.exe!Player::update+0x2a"  ->  module "game.exe", function "Player::update", offset 0x2A
"ntdll.dll+0x1F00"              ->  module "ntdll.dll", function "", offset 0x1F00
"no offset here"                ->  nullopt
```

Function names can contain `::`, `<`, `>` and spaces, but never `!` or `+`.
hints: `std::optional<T>` (from `<optional>`) holds either a `T` or nothing. `return value;` gives back a filled one and `return std::nullopt;` an empty one. A caller tests it with `if (result)` (or `result.has_value()`) and reads the value inside with `*result`.
Find the last `+0x` (or `+0X`): everything after it is the offset's hex digits; everything before it is `module` or `module!function`.
Convert the hex digits yourself, one at a time: multiply what you have by 16 and add the digit's value. Reject any character that is not a hex digit.
